Omar T.: Heads up  carrier just emailed that my child's enrollment was denied due to SSN mismatch. I think I typed the number wrong when I added them during open enroll. What do I need to fix this?
Lina (People Ops): Sorry you're dealing with that, Omar. :( We can correct it, but carriers require verification. First step: gather the correct SSN documentation + proof of identity for the dependent (birth cert or passport).
Omar T.: Ugh ok. I have the birth certificate scanned at home. The SSN card is at my filing cabinet at home — can I take a photo and upload?
Amrita K.: Photo of the SSN card is OK if legible. Carriers sometimes want an attestation too if there's any discrepancy. We'll ask you to sign a short attestation confirming the corrected SSN submission and that you authorize us to resubmit to the carrier.
Ken L.: Payroll note: if coverage is reopened retro, premiums may need to be adjusted. If the carrier paid claims that were denied because of the mismatch, that can complicate things. We'll coordinate once Benefits confirms acceptance.
Omar T.: Is there a secure upload link? I don't want to put SSN images in email.
people-ops-bot: Secure upload link generated: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload/OT-1889004567 (expires in 14 days).
Lina (People Ops): Use that link. Choose "Dependent documentation - SSN correction" and include the correct SSN in the form notes. Upload: 1) clear photo of SSN card OR SSA printout, 2) birth certificate or passport, 3) short signed attestation (we can provide a template).
Omar T.: Template would be great. Also, will my child's coverage be reinstated retroactive to the original effective date if carrier accepts?
Benefits Admin: If carrier accepts the correction, coverage is typically reinstated retroactive to the original enrollment effective date. If claims were processed and denied, the carrier may reprocess after we resubmit. Timeline varies by carrier (3-30 business days).
Amrita K.: If carrier rejects the correction we might need additional docs (court decree, SS-5 proof of application). We'll escalate if that happens.
Omar T.: OK. Can you post the attestation template here so I can sign and upload?
Lina (People Ops): Attestation template: "I, [employee name], confirm that the Social Security Number submitted for dependent [name] was incorrect on [date]. I attest that the attached SSN card (or SSA documentation) shows the correct SSN and I authorize Redwood Benefits to correct and resubmit enrollment to the insurance carrier. Signed: [signature] Date: [date]"
Omar T.: Thanks. Anything else I should include in the upload notes?
Lina (People Ops): Put the original enrollment date and the plan names. Example note: "SSN correction for [child name], originally enrolled 2026-02-10, plans: Medical PPO, Dental Core. Correct SSN: XXX-XX-XXXX. Uploading SSN card + birth cert + attestation."
Ken L.: If payroll withheld premium based on the original enrollment and carrier later backdates coverage, payroll will adjust deductions and process an offset/refund if needed. If you see anything odd on paystub, tag @Ken.
Omar T.: Uploaded SSN pic + birth cert + signed attestation.
people-ops-bot: Case created: PO-7555 - Dependent SSN correction. Benefits admin notified.
Benefits Admin: Received. We'll validate and resubmit to carrier today. Expect confirmation DM here when carrier responds.
Omar T.: Really appreciate the quick help. :pray:
